hero.headline: US approved Nvidia chip sales to Chinese firm with empty office and ties to blacklisted entity
hero.body:
The Commerce Department approved Nvidia to sell its H200 AI chips to a Chinese company that appears to have no real operations and whose owners have connections to a blacklisted firm, according to a New York Times investigation. New Matrix, created 17 months ago, lists an address where the Times found empty offices with wires hanging from the ceiling. A building directory did not include the company, and property management staff said they had no record of it.

What limited information exists about New Matrix raises security concerns. The company's owners have ties to a Chinese private equity firm that the US government blacklisted in 2024. The Times reported this is part of a broader pattern in which companies connected to entities facing national security trade restrictions have been approved to purchase Nvidia chips.

Nvidia had been barred from selling chips to China during the Biden administration. The Trump administration loosened those restrictions after Nvidia agreed to give the government a 15 percent cut of all sales. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang also conducted an intense lobbying campaign and was reportedly targeted by China's Ministry of State Security in a spying operation.

The approvals have raised questions about whether the Commerce Department and Nvidia are adequately vetting Chinese firms cleared to handle the company's advanced AI chips. The H200 chips are among Nvidia's most powerful processors for artificial intelligence applications.

cards.headline: Ukraine Launches 400 Drones Toward Moscow in Major Attack
cards.teaser: Ukrainian forces conducted one of their largest drone operations against the Russian capital as President Zelenskyy faces domestic pressure.
cards.body:
Ukraine fired approximately 400 drones toward Moscow in a significant escalation of its air campaign against Russia. The attack represents one of the largest single drone operations Ukraine has conducted against the Russian capital since the war began.

The strike follows a major Russian assault on Ukrainian cities, including Kyiv, where Russia launched 41 missiles and 125 attack drones. The escalating exchanges mark an intensification of aerial operations on both sides, with each country targeting the other's infrastructure and military assets.

cards.headline: Paraguay's president impeached, arrested after bank collapse left millions unable to access savings
cards.teaser: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña was impeached and placed under house arrest Friday after lawmakers unanimously voted to remove him from office over the collapse of Ueno Bank, a
cards.body:
Paraguay's President Santiago Peña was impeached and placed under house arrest Friday after lawmakers unanimously voted to remove him from office over the collapse of Ueno Bank, a

The bank's demise has left more than half of Paraguay's population—an estimated three million depositors—unable to access their savings and pensions, prompting widespread protests particularly in the capital, Asunción. Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in as interim president and will serve until 2028.

cards.headline: Secret Service arrests man near White House with guns who said voices told him to kill Trump
cards.teaser: The Secret Service arrested a man Thursday night near the White House after officers found him in a parked vehicle with multiple guns and ammunition and he told them he heard voice
cards.body:
The Secret Service arrested a man Thursday night near the White House after officers found him in a parked vehicle with multiple guns and ammunition and he told them he heard voice

Officers approached Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos after observing him acting suspiciously in a parked car, according to a Department of Homeland Security statement. Chrinos described hearing voices instructing him to come to Washington and kill the president, the statement said.

cards.headline: Wave of bomb threats and cyberattacks across Europe raises questions about coordination
cards.body:
A series of bomb threats targeting airlines and cyberattacks on critical infrastructure across Europe has disrupted everyday life and heightened security concerns, though the perpetrators remain unidentified. The incidents have affected multiple sectors, including aviation, healthcare, and food supply systems.

Cyberattacks targeted European refrigeration systems and critical health infrastructure, including a French blood bank. Security researchers reported that hackers had probed Europe's commercial refrigeration networks weeks before the attacks occurred. A health intelligence-sharing group issued warnings to the healthcare industry following the breach of the French blood bank.

The airline industry faced a wave of bomb hoaxes that forced flight disruptions. The attacks on freezer systems caused meltdowns at facilities across the continent, threatening stored medical supplies and perishable goods.

Authorities have not publicly identified who is responsible for the coordinated disruptions. The nature and timing of the incidents have raised questions about whether the attacks are linked and whether they represent a broader campaign targeting European infrastructure.

cards.headline: Heavy rains flood tens of thousands of tents housing displaced Gazans
cards.teaser: A United Nations official said nearly everyone in the territory needs help as the rainy season begins.
cards.body:
Heavy rains flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced residents in Gaza, leaving some without shelter, according to a United Nations official and the Hamas-run government. The Hamas-run government said about 70,000 tents were flooded and that collapsing walls and roofs caused injuries, some critical. Residents used pots and pans to clear water from tents.

Jonathan Veitch, the Unicef representative for Palestine, said the situation was worsened by Israeli restrictions on entry of heavy machinery and supplies. About 90 percent of Gaza residents have been displaced by the Israeli war against Hamas, many multiple times, with limited access to clean water and sanitation. Aid agencies said the situation is likely to worsen with the rainy season.

cards.headline: Trump replaces chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller after GOP midterm losses
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump announced Friday that he is replacing Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff with longtime adviser Stephen Miller, following Republican losses in Tuesday'
cards.body:
President Donald Trump announced Friday that he is replacing Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff with longtime adviser Stephen Miller, following Republican losses in Tuesday's midterm elections. Wiles submitted her resignation Thursday night after Trump blamed her for the election results in which Republicans lost control of Congress. Trump will install Miller, currently deputy chief of staff, in the position starting Monday.

Wiles had offered to resign for two days before Trump accepted her decision Friday. A source who spoke with Wiles said Trump did not directly ask for her resignation but could not stop blaming her rather than himself for the midterm losses. The source said Wiles recognized that if she could not change Trump's view, there was no reason to remain.

Miller, who also served in Trump's first administration, has been working on plans to maintain executive authority despite large Democratic majorities in Congress. A Trump adviser described Miller as a wartime adviser needed to prepare for Democratic investigations. Miller was an architect of Trump's aggressive use of executive power during his first hundred days in office.

Wiles was Trump's longest-serving chief of staff and the first woman to hold the position. She earned an extraordinary level of trust from Trump and often served as the last person he consulted before major decisions. Her influence stemmed from managing his 2016 Florida campaign and his political comeback after the Jan. 6 riot. Wiles had privately opposed the war in Iran and hardline immigration enforcement championed by Miller, policies that contributed to Tuesday's Republican losses.

cards.headline: New Zealand election produces no clear winner, coalition talks ahead
cards.teaser: National won the most seats but fell short of a majority, while Labour refused to concede as a new centrist party emerged as potential kingmaker.
cards.body:
New Zealand's general election on Saturday produced no outright winner, leaving Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's centre-right National Party and opposition leader Chris Hipkins's Labour Party preparing for coalition negotiations. National won 42 seats and Labour took 36, both short of the 61 needed for a majority in parliament, according to preliminary results.

The centrist Opportunity Party crossed the 5 percent threshold to enter parliament for the first time and said it would negotiate with whichever major party won the most seats. Official results are due November 27. The campaign focused heavily on cost of living and unemployment, with preliminary results showing historically low combined support for the two major parties at around 60 percent.

cards.headline: UK cannot selectively adopt EU single market rules, Barnier says
cards.teaser: Former EU Brexit negotiator says Britain must accept all four freedoms, including free movement of people, to rejoin the single market.
cards.body:
Former EU Brexit negotiator Michel Barnier told the BBC that Britain cannot selectively adopt elements of the EU single market as the prime minister considers closer ties with Europe. Barnier said EU members would require the UK to accept all four freedoms—including free movement of people—to gain market access, rejecting any possibility of picking and choosing conditions.

Barnier led EU Brexit negotiations from 2016 to 2021. Prime Minister Burnham said in July he could pursue rejoining the single market but ruled out major changes before the next election. Both sides plan to discuss deals on food standards, youth visas, and carbon trading at a Brussels meeting in 10 days.

cards.headline: Italian foreign minister says pro-Russian hackers leaked his personal data in retaliation for Ukraine support
cards.teaser: Antonio Tajani says cybercriminals published his information on the dark web and targeted his family. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni backed the claim.
cards.body:
Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said cybercriminals published his personal data on the dark web and targeted his family because of Italy's support for Ukraine. Tajani said the hackers exposed him to threats and intimidation, calling Italy's position on Ukraine the political reason he was targeted. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni blamed pro-Russian hackers and expressed concern about the sale of confidential information about institutional representatives.

Tajani, who is also deputy prime minister, said the government was taking the threats seriously. Moscow has not publicly responded to the allegations. Italy has provided humanitarian and military support to Ukraine in its war against Russia.

Paraguay's President Santiago Peña was impeached and placed under house arrest Friday after lawmakers unanimously voted to remove him from office over the collapse of Ueno Bank, a

hero.headline: Hamilton and Verstappen to start from back of grid at São Paulo Grand Prix
hero.body:
Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Red Bull's Max Verstappen will start from the back of the grid at Sunday's São Paulo Grand Prix after power-unit changes resulted in penalties for both drivers. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Mercedes' George Russell will also face grid penalties, with Leclerc dropping 10 places and Russell five.

Hamilton initially faced a 10-place penalty for exceeding his power-unit allowance for the season. However, after a new internal combustion engine fitted Saturday morning failed during final practice, Ferrari installed an entire new power unit, leading to the more severe penalty. Verstappen received an all-new engine after Red Bull discovered problems following Friday practice.

Leclerc and Russell both fitted new internal combustion engines. Leclerc's larger penalty reflects that Ferrari exceeded the limit of four engines per season on his car for the first time, while Russell had already surpassed that threshold. Verstappen previously won the São Paulo Grand Prix from 17th on the grid after an engine penalty in wet conditions.

Qualifying is expected to be wet after rain began about an hour before the session. Rain is forecast to continue overnight and could occur at any point on race day. Formula 1 also announced Saturday that São Paulo's Interlagos circuit extended its contract to host a grand prix until 2035.

cards.headline: New Zealand defeats Scotland 43-21 in rugby Nations Championship
cards.teaser: The All Blacks scored seven tries at Murrayfield, dominating the second half after Scotland's Ewan Ashman completed a first-half hat-trick.
cards.body:
New Zealand defeated Scotland 43-21 in a Nations Championship rugby match at Murrayfield. Scotland hooker Ewan Ashman scored a historic first-half hat-trick, keeping the match close at halftime with New Zealand leading 24-21. Beauden Barrett scored twice for the All Blacks, while Wallace Sititi, Ethan de Groot, Codie Taylor, Josh Moorby, and Asafo Aumua also crossed for tries.

New Zealand dominated the second half, outscoring Scotland 19-0 after the break. The victory marked New Zealand's 32nd win against Scotland in 34 Tests dating back to 1905, with two draws. Scotland struggled with penalties and a yellow card to captain Sione Tuipulotu as the All Blacks controlled possession in the final 40 minutes.

cards.headline: Secret Service arrests man near White House with guns who said voices told him to kill Trump
cards.teaser: The Secret Service arrested a man Thursday night near the White House after officers found him in a parked vehicle with multiple guns and ammunition and he told them he heard voice

The Secret Service arrested a man Thursday night near the White House after officers found him in a parked vehicle with multiple guns and ammunition and he told them he heard voice

cards.headline: Data center opposition drives Democratic midterm gains
cards.teaser: Backlash against data center construction helped Democrats win key races, with voters opposing new facilities in their communities by roughly 3-to-1.
cards.body:
Opposition to data center construction emerged as a significant factor in Democratic victories during the midterm elections, helping the party win statewide in Texas for the first time since 1994. About a quarter of voters said AI and data centers were crucial to their vote, according to CNN polling, while voters opposed building data centers in their communities by roughly 3-to-1.

Michigan Representative-elect Will Lawrence, who flipped a Republican-held House seat, centered his campaign on data center opposition and described the backlash as overwhelming and bipartisan. Texas state Representative-elect James Talarico won Kaufman County by 1 percentage point while winning statewide by 12 points.

cards.headline: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production in Texas next year, Musk says
cards.teaser: Tesla will wind down production of its Cybertruck vehicles at its Texas factory next year, Elon Musk said Friday. Musk did not specify whether the company plans to stop making the
cards.body:
Tesla will wind down production of its Cybertruck vehicles at its Texas factory next year, Elon Musk said Friday. Musk did not specify whether the company plans to stop making the

Musk did not specify whether the company plans to stop making the trucks entirely or shift production elsewhere, but said the decision was to make room for building more of its self-driving Cybercab cars. Wes Morrill, the project's lead engineer, wrote on social media that Cybertruck was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab, appearing to suggest the vehicle is being discontinued.

cards.headline: Alternative cosmology model proposing 26.7 billion-year-old universe passes major observational tests
cards.teaser: A University of Ottawa study finds a model requiring neither dark matter nor dark energy holds up against key astronomical data.
cards.body:
An alternative cosmology model proposing the universe is 26.7 billion years old and requires neither dark matter nor dark energy has passed several major observational tests, according to a University of Ottawa study published in the journal Universe. Researchers Rajendra Gupta and Nikolaos Samaras tested the model, which suggests evolving fundamental constants could explain effects typically attributed to dark matter and dark energy.

The model's predictions matched observations for light element formation after the Big Bang, cosmic expansion measurements, and galaxy rotation curves from 175 galaxies. The researchers report it could also explain unusually mature early galaxies by allowing about 4.6 billion years for formation at cosmic dawn rather than the standard model's 300 million years.

cards.headline: Small asteroid temporarily captured as Earth's mini-moon will break free by early 2027
cards.teaser: A roughly one- to two-meter-wide asteroid named 2026 QQ8 has been orbiting Earth since April.
cards.body:
Astronomers have confirmed that a small asteroid named 2026 QQ8 has been temporarily captured by Earth's gravity and is orbiting the planet as a mini-moon. The roughly one- to two-meter-wide space rock entered Earth's gravitational sphere of influence in April and was first observed in August by Hungarian astronomer Krisztián Sárneczky. The International Astronomical Union's Minor Planet Center confirmed it as a natural object on October 29 after follow-up observations ruled out an artificial origin.

The asteroid is expected to remain temporarily bound to Earth through December before breaking free and continuing its orbit around the Sun in early 2027. Its closest predicted distance during this period is about 568,000 kilometers, roughly one-and-a-half times the average Earth-Moon distance, and it poses no impact threat.

cards.headline: Researchers convert wind turbine blades into graphene and silicon carbide using flash heating
cards.teaser: A new method heats hard-to-recycle blades to 2,000°C in seconds, transforming them into valuable manufacturing materials.
cards.body:
Researchers have developed a method to recycle wind turbine blades by subjecting them to flash joule heating, according to a study published in Chem Circularity. The process heats blades made from silica-containing fiberglass and carbon-rich polymer resin to approximately 2,000 degrees Celsius in seconds, converting them into silicon carbide and graphene.

At such high temperatures, carbon reacts with silica to form silicon carbide, a hard and heat-resistant material, while carbon also reorganizes into graphene, known for its strength and conductivity. The research team found that adding the broken-down blades to other materials before heating improved the usefulness of the resulting material for creating new rotor blades.

cards.headline: Sequoia Capital shuts down pioneering scout investment program
cards.teaser: The firm's decision to end its 17-year-old program signals broader industry doubts about the venture scouting model.
cards.body:
Sequoia Capital announced it is shutting down its scout program, which for 17 years allowed select founders and operators to write checks on the firm's behalf. The firm framed the decision as part of a broader effort to focus resources, closing its London office as well.

The move suggests growing industry consensus that the scouting model has reached its limits. Andreessen Horowitz has similarly revamped its scout program to concentrate on fewer, more active participants with larger budgets. Some observers note that leading venture firms now attract top founders directly, reducing the need for scouts except in early-stage or niche markets.

cards.headline: World of Warcraft: Forever sets franchise launch record
cards.teaser: Blizzard confirms the classic-style relaunch achieved the highest peak concurrent players in the game's history.
cards.body:
Blizzard Entertainment confirmed that World of Warcraft: Forever recorded the biggest launch in the franchise's history by peak concurrent players, surpassing even Wrath of the Lich King from nearly two decades ago. The company also reported the highest number of returning players in the game's history.

World of Warcraft: Forever is a reimagined version of the original game with minimal handholding, enhanced risk-reward mechanics, reduced convenience features, and improved visual quality. The release includes thousands of new quests set in an alternative timeline approximately one year before the original base game.

cards.headline: British soldier court-martialed after ignoring order to remove SIM card led to phone hack and blackmail
cards.teaser: A corporal deployed to Estonia kept his SIM card active despite orders, resulting in his phone being hacked and nude photos stolen.
cards.body:
Daniel Barton-Kennedy, a British Army corporal, was court-martialed and sentenced to 10 months in detention after disobeying orders to remove his phone's SIM card during deployment to Estonia in January 2026. The soldier was briefed multiple times on operational security procedures requiring troops to remove SIM cards and disable location settings before and during Exercise Eastern Warrior, held approximately 90 miles west of the Russian border.

Barton-Kennedy's failure to comply resulted in his phone being hacked and nude photos stolen, which were then used to blackmail him. He pleaded guilty to disobeying a lawful command and was reduced in rank. The case was first reported by Estonian newspaper Eesti Ekspress.

hero.headline: UConn beats Michigan 85-77 in rare opening-week rematch of last season's NCAA title game
hero.body:
Connecticut defeated Michigan 85-77 on Friday night at TD Garden in Boston, marking the earliest rematch between the previous season's men's national championship game participants since Duke and UConn met in November 1999. The fourth-ranked Huskies defeated the 16th-ranked Wolverines in a game that featured 59 free throws and lasted nearly two and a half hours. It was only the second time in the past 17 seasons that the men's title game was replayed the following season.

UConn guard Silas Demary Jr. and Braylon Mullins combined for 44 points, 11 rebounds and three steals to lead the Huskies. Mullins scored a game-high 23 points, while Demary contributed 21 points and has 12 assists with zero turnovers through two games this season. Both players struggled in last season's championship game, with Demary scoring just two points while playing on a severely sprained ankle. Demary told CBS Sports he had not watched footage of that loss and had the rematch circled since the defeat.

Connecticut shot 40.9 percent from three-point range and made 30 of 36 free throws. Michigan was led by sophomore Trey McKenney, who scored all of his team-high 22 points in the second half, but the Wolverines shot just 7-for-28 from beyond the arc. The loss was Michigan's first game against a ranked opponent this early in a season since 1993, and the first time the Wolverines failed to start a season 2-0 since 2000-01. Michigan coach Mike Boynton is in his first season after Dusty May left to take the Dallas Mavericks job during the offseason.

UConn coach Dan Hurley said the victory was critical given the Huskies' challenging schedule ahead, which includes games against Ohio State, Arizona and Duke later this month. The win extended Connecticut's streak to 10 consecutive regular-season, neutral-site victories over ranked opponents. Freshman Colben Landrew added eight rebounds in 22 minutes, and shooting guard Solo Ball, initially expected to miss the season with a broken wrist, could return within the next month.

cards.headline: Verstappen, Hamilton, Leclerc and Russell handed grid penalties for Sao Paulo Grand Prix
cards.teaser: Four drivers will start at the back or mid-grid after engine changes, while F1 extends Interlagos contract through 2035.
cards.body:
Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton will start from the back of the grid at Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix after exceeding their power-unit allowances for the season. Hamilton initially faced a 10-place penalty but received a larger drop after Ferrari fitted an entire new power unit following an engine failure in final practice Saturday morning. Verstappen had a new engine fitted after Red Bull discovered problems following Friday practice.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc will drop 10 places and Mercedes' George Russell five places after both fitted new internal combustion engines. Meanwhile, Formula One announced Saturday that Interlagos had extended its contract to host the Brazilian Grand Prix through 2035.

cards.headline: New Zealand defeats Scotland 43-21 at Murrayfield in Nations Championship
cards.teaser: All Blacks extend dominant head-to-head record despite first-half hat-trick from Scotland's Ewan Ashman.
cards.body:
New Zealand defeated Scotland 43-21 at Murrayfield in a Nations Championship match, extending their head-to-head record to 32 wins and two draws since 1905. Scotland hooker Ewan Ashman scored a historic first-half hat-trick, and the teams were separated by just three points at halftime with seven combined tries.

The All Blacks dominated the second half, outscoring Scotland 19-0 after the break. Beauden Barrett scored twice for New Zealand, while Wallace Sititi, Ethan de Groot, Codie Taylor, Josh Moorby, and Asafo Aumua also crossed for tries. Scotland captain Sione Tuipulotu received a yellow card during New Zealand's second-half surge.

cards.headline: Ponga returns from broken arm to power New Zealand into Rugby League World Cup final
cards.teaser: The full-back played just 23 days after breaking his forearm and requiring surgery, helping the Kiwis defeat Tonga 34-10.
cards.body:
Kalyn Ponga returned just 23 days after breaking his left forearm and undergoing surgery to lead New Zealand to a 34-10 victory over Tonga in the Rugby League World Cup semi-final. The 28-year-old full-back, who sustained the injury during New Zealand's tournament opener against Australia on October 15, was directly involved in four of the Kiwis' six tries and made a crucial try-saving tackle.

The victory sends New Zealand to their first World Cup final in 13 years. Coach Stacey Jones praised Ponga as tough and said the decision to play him came after final training sessions confirmed his readiness. New Zealand will face the winner of the other semi-final next Sunday as they pursue their second title after winning in 2008.

cards.headline: Rahm takes one-shot lead into final round in Abu Dhabi
cards.teaser: Jon Rahm holds a one-shot lead over Tyrrell Hatton and Francesco Laporta heading into the final round, with Rory McIlroy two shots back.
cards.body:
Jon Rahm holds a one-shot lead heading into the final round of the Abu Dhabi Championship after shooting a six-under-par 66 on Saturday at Yas Links. The Spaniard stands at 18 under par, one shot ahead of Tyrrell Hatton and Francesco Laporta, who both carded 67s.

Rory McIlroy sits two shots back at 16 under after a third-round 67 that included eight birdies but also a double bogey at the 10th hole. Rahm is seeking his first solo tournament victory since winning the Masters in 2023. Adam Scott is in fifth place at 15 under.

cards.headline: MLB awards Platinum Gloves to Crow-Armstrong, Bellinger as Cubs, Blue Jays win team honors
cards.teaser: Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and Cody Bellinger received Platinum Gloves, while Chicago and Toronto earned team Gold Glove awards for top defensive performance.
cards.body:
Pete Crow-Armstrong received the Platinum Glove along with his Gold Glove and Fielding Bible Award for best defensive player of 2026. The Cubs center fielder is expected to capture National League MVP honors on November 12. Cody Bellinger also won a Platinum Glove.

Rawlings awarded team Gold Glove honors to the Cubs and Blue Jays for the best overall defensive clubs in each league. The Cubs led the majors with 72 Outs Above Average and plus-115 Defensive Runs Saved. Toronto posted 15 OAA and plus-51 DRS. Both franchises have won the team Gold Glove three times since Rawlings introduced the award in 2020.

cards.headline: England bowler Josh Tongue ruled out of Australia tour with toe injury
cards.teaser: The fast bowler will miss white-ball matches after suffering the injury in Pakistan last month.
cards.body:
England fast bowler Josh Tongue has been ruled out of the upcoming white-ball tour of Australia with a toe injury. The 28-year-old suffered the injury in Pakistan last month and will return to the UK for further assessment, missing the one-day and T20 matches that begin with an ODI in Perth on November 13. Tongue, who has taken 46 wickets in 17 matches this year, is expected to return for the three-match Test series in South Africa in December.

In a warm-up match in Perth, Adil Rashid took four wickets as England beat Western Australia by 92 runs. The 38-year-old spinner took 4-35 while Jofra Archer added 3-34, bowling out the hosts for 159 after England posted 251.

hero.headline: Richard Lloyd, Television guitarist whose interplay with Tom Verlaine shaped Marquee Moon, dies at 75
hero.body:
Richard Lloyd, the Television co-founder and guitarist whose intricate interplay with Tom Verlaine helped define punk-era guitar work on the band's 1977 debut Marquee Moon, has died at 75. Lloyd died Saturday morning at his home in Chattanooga, Tennessee, from cholangiocarcinoma, a bile duct cancer, his family said in a statement. His wife Sheila and his dog Willie Mays were with him. Lloyd was diagnosed with the cancer in March 2026.

Television stood apart from many punk contemporaries through the twin guitar attack of Lloyd and Verlaine, who died in 2023. While peers favored power chords, Lloyd and Verlaine developed an intricate interplay of riffs and licks inspired by jazz, art-rock, and jam bands. Lloyd described their partnership to The Stranger in 2015, saying he saw that Verlaine had something he was missing and vice versa. Lloyd said he brought the fleshing out of songs and a rock and roll heart, playing melody during verses while Verlaine sang.

On Marquee Moon, Lloyd pushed to double-track some of his guitar parts, insisting to Verlaine and co-producer Andy Johns that he could replicate intricate passages note-for-note to give the record depth beyond a live recording. He selectively used the technique across the album and laid down eight guitar tracks on "Guiding Light" to make it sound powerful and thick. Despite critical regard, Marquee Moon failed commercially, and Television broke up in 1978 after releasing Adventure. The band's output consisted of those two albums plus a 1992 reunion record.

Lloyd released nine solo albums between 1979 and 2018, toured regularly, worked as a session musician with artists including Matthew Sweet and John Doe, and gave guitar lessons. He rejoined Television for the 1992 reunion and again in the early 2000s but left before a 2007 tour marking Marquee Moon's 30th anniversary. Lloyd told The Stranger he got into music not for money but to become a renowned guitarist who made an irrevocable impact on rock and roll history.

cards.headline: Director Takashi Yamazaki Fulfills Childhood Dream With King Ghidorah in 'Godzilla Minus Zero'
cards.teaser: The Oscar-winning filmmaker discusses bringing the iconic three-headed kaiju to his hometown and the VFX challenges behind key sequences.
cards.body:
The Oscar-winning filmmaker discusses bringing the iconic three-headed kaiju to his hometown and the VFX challenges behind key sequences.

Director Takashi Yamazaki said bringing King Ghidorah to the screen in "Godzilla Minus Zero" fulfilled a childhood dream of seeing his hometown destroyed by the iconic kaiju. Yamazaki, who won an Oscar for visual effects on "Godzilla Minus One," set a key sequence in Matsumoto City, where he was born and raised, after being disappointed as a child when the monster only flew over the city in its 1964 debut film.

cards.headline: Dolly Parton's estate manager drops lawsuit against her nephew
cards.teaser: Danny Nozell filed the case less than a month after Parton's death, alleging threats and intimidation by Bryan Seaver.
cards.body:
The manager of Dolly Parton's estate has dropped a lawsuit against her nephew Bryan Seaver that alleged threats, intimidation, and coercion. Danny Nozell, who heads the company managing Parton's business interests, filed the civil case less than a month after the country music star's death in August at age 80. The lawsuit included allegations that Seaver, Parton's former head of security, threatened to damage her brand while demanding payment from the estate. A judge had granted a temporary restraining order.

Seaver denied the allegations. His attorneys said in a statement he was grateful to put the misunderstanding behind him so the family can grieve peacefully. Seaver, the son of Parton's sister Cassie, owns a security firm that provided protection to Parton for the final 20 years of her life.

cards.headline: Deep Purple singer Ian Gillan undergoes successful surgery after medical emergency
cards.teaser: The vocalist says he is now resting to make a complete recovery after a health issue forced the band to cancel its European tour.
cards.body:
Deep Purple singer Ian Gillan said he underwent successful surgery following a medical emergency that forced the band to postpone its European tour. Gillan told fans on social media that he must now rest to ensure a complete recovery before returning to work. He apologized for the inconvenience caused by the cancellations.

The band postponed shows in Germany and canceled the remainder of its European tour, which had been scheduled to run through late November, after Gillan was hospitalized in Leipzig with an unspecified health issue. Deep Purple's Latin America tour is scheduled to begin in early December in Brazil.

cards.headline: Alanis Morissette comes out as pansexual on podcast
cards.teaser: The singer disclosed her sexual orientation during the Nov. 3 episode of the Handsome podcast.
cards.body:
Alanis Morissette came out as pansexual during the Nov. 3 episode of the Handsome podcast, co-hosted by Tig Notaro, Fortune Feimster, and Mae Martin. When Feimster asked whether past relationships with men made her want to be a lesbian, Morissette replied that she is pansexual. After Notaro expressed surprise, Morissette confirmed the disclosure.

Morissette has been married to Mario Treadway since 2010, and they have three children. The Canadian singer-songwriter found fame in 1995 with Jagged Little Pill and was inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame this year.

cards.headline: Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult screen-test for James Bond role
cards.teaser: The actors auditioned in late October for director Denis Villeneuve as the studio's search for Daniel Craig's replacement continues.
cards.body:
Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult screen-tested for the role of James Bond in late October, according to multiple reports. Pattinson, who stars in The Batman series and recently worked with director Denis Villeneuve on Dune: Part Three, auditioned for the role alongside Hoult, who appeared in the Superman and X-Men franchises.

The two actors join previously reported candidates Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, and Josh O'Connor in the search for Daniel Craig's replacement. Amazon MGM Studios, which will produce the films under Villeneuve's direction, has not commented on the audition process that began in May.

cards.headline: Monty Don presents final Gardeners' World episode after two decades
cards.teaser: The BBC horticulturalist signed off Friday from Longmeadow garden, thanking viewers for sharing his gardening journey since 2003.
cards.body:
Monty Don presented his final episode of Gardeners' World on Friday, concluding more than two decades as host of the BBC gardening series. The 71-year-old horticulturalist signed off from Longmeadow garden, where the show has been based for 16 years, calling it a "privilege and pleasure" to share his garden experiences with viewers. Don replaced Alan Titchmarsh in 2003.

Don will remain part of the presenting team for next year's Royal Horticultural Society Chelsea Flower Show and will appear in two winter specials airing before Christmas. The BBC has not yet named his successor for Gardeners' World, though regular co-presenters Frances Tophill and Adam Frost have been cited as contenders.

hero.headline: Trump replaces chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller after GOP midterm losses
hero.teaser: President Donald Trump announced Friday that he is replacing Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff with longtime adviser Stephen Miller, following Republican losses in Tuesday'
hero.body:
President Donald Trump announced Friday that he is replacing Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff with longtime adviser Stephen Miller, following Republican losses in Tuesday's midterm elections. Wiles submitted her resignation Thursday night after Trump blamed her for the election results in which Republicans lost control of Congress. Trump will install Miller, currently deputy chief of staff, in the position starting Monday.

Wiles had offered to resign for two days before Trump accepted her decision Friday. A source who spoke with Wiles said Trump did not directly ask for her resignation but could not stop blaming her rather than himself for the midterm losses. The source said Wiles recognized that if she could not change Trump's view, there was no reason to remain.

Miller, who also served in Trump's first administration, has been working on plans to maintain executive authority despite large Democratic majorities in Congress. A Trump adviser described Miller as a wartime adviser needed to prepare for Democratic investigations. Miller was an architect of Trump's aggressive use of executive power during his first hundred days in office.

Wiles was Trump's longest-serving chief of staff and the first woman to hold the position. She earned an extraordinary level of trust from Trump and often served as the last person he consulted before major decisions. Her influence stemmed from managing his 2016 Florida campaign and his political comeback after the Jan. 6 riot. Wiles had privately opposed the war in Iran and hardline immigration enforcement championed by Miller, policies that contributed to Tuesday's Republican losses.
